description:
FILED s409 (Fable) at the USER's request, end of session: "please write that we
should make a plan to reorganize all that, it seems much too complex?  Can it
be done in a simpler way.  But that is next time."  => NEXT FABLE SESSION opens
with THIS: a plan to reorganize the two-compiler entanglement, asking FIRST
whether it can be done in a simpler way than E5.1-E5.5 (9-17 sessions,
docs/v2-endgame-plan.md) before executing anything.

WHAT WAS MEASURED s409 (do not re-derive):
  * One PIPELINE since s356 (E4.1).  Inside it, TWO expression generators and
    v1's statement layer are still live: tools/v2-census.pl over the 111-file
    corpus = 2268 native / 16898 seam expressions (88.2% fall back to v1's
    ExprToCL via _parse_expression_form) + 1050 seam STATEMENTS (local 310,
    use 229, no 119, BEGIN 119, sub 106, Plain 42, push 33, require 30, delete
    14, return 11, my 10, ...).  Unchanged since s316t.
  * The strings->forms conversion is DONE: ExprToCL has 41 *_form generators,
    ZERO string gen_* subs, 11 raw()/raw_wrap() residues.  ExprToCL2 is a
    268-line arithmetic fast path (scalars/numbers/binops/parens/a few W11
    element reads), NOT a destination -- E5.4 folds it INTO ExprToCL.
  * ExprToCL reaches the v1 Parser object through only 4 accessors (lex_home,
    eval_mode, {_eval_env_used}, can); PExpr through 11 -- mainly the embedded
    block callbacks (parse_block_as_function x1363/corpus, parse_block_to_cl_*,
    parse_hash_block_*) and parse_expr_to_tree.
  * THE COMPLEXITY IS ENTANGLEMENT, NOT TRANSLATION: (1) expression codegen
    _emit()s top-level forms (anon-block defuns for block-prototype args, sort
    comparators) into the v1 Parser's SECTIONS/BUCKETS -- a global output
    buffer -- so Parser2::_lower_expr wraps every fallback in a ~40-line
    save/redirect/drain/restore dance (x16898 per corpus); (2) expressions
    contain BLOCKS (map/grep/sort/eval/do/sub bodies) that call back into a
    STATEMENT compiler -- v1's, wherever Parser2::lower_embedded_block still
    declines -- which is why 126/139 Parser.pm subs are live; (3) 12 statement
    kinds go to v1's _process_* handlers WHOLE (each = ten months of quirks,
    the sweep the only oracle; calibrated 2-3 classes/session); (4) PExpr's
    cleanup_for_parsing MUTATES the shared PPI tokens, so the seam snapshots
    and restores token state around the native attempt -- and 88% OF
    EXPRESSIONS ARE PARSED TWICE (native attempt fails, fallback re-parses);
    (5) every change in the region ships behind corpus-diff + full sweep +
    gate (~1 h) because the last three "mechanical" edits there silently
    dropped statements (#138 family).

STARTING HYPOTHESIS FOR THE SIMPLER WAY (Fable, s409, unverified): reorder --
E5.4 FIRST (fold ExprToCL2's branches into ExprToCL, ONE parse, ONE generator,
delete the native attempt + snapshot/restore: ~2-3 sessions, and a compile-time
win from ending the double parse); then E5.1 (one SeamSession object owning
the bucket dance) + E5.2 (lower_embedded_block stops declining); E5.3 (the 12
statement classes) LAST and class-by-class, possibly post-v0.1.  And ask
whether the bucket/_emit side channel can simply be RETURNED (a form plus a
list of hoisted forms) instead of drained -- that would delete the dance
rather than encapsulate it.  Also ask whether the 12 classes need porting at
all if v1's handlers can be called through one stateless entry (E5.1) --
i.e. whether "one compiler" for the release means one GENERATOR (cheap) or
zero v1 lines (E5.3, the long tail).

Cross-refs: docs/v2-endgame-plan.md E5 (the 9-17 estimate), docs/v2-target-
architecture.md §4-5 (module map + the 16-29 total), docs/compiler-
duplication-review-s386.md (the 88% headline, the sequenced plan), task #153
(Option B: term grammar inside PExpr -- does NOT retire v1 by construction,
DECIDED s398), #303 (dead code batch, done), #243/#255 (E4.1, done).
Not on the v0.1 critical path as planned (release-plan-v0.1.md); the USER may
decide otherwise once the plan exists.

ADDED by the USER, end of s409: "Also add that we should do a comprehensive
search for doubled code.  It seems lots of small bits can be extracted to
subs."  => part of the SAME plan (next Fable session): a systematic
duplicate-code search over Pl/**, cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, tools/**, and the
runners -- not the s386 call-trace kind (which found DEAD mass), but the
"same 5-20 lines written twice, three times" kind: e.g. the six statement
modifiers were inlined as a regex in FOUR parser sites until s408 (#374a);
the bucket save/drain/restore dance exists in TWO copies (_lower_expr and
_fallback_stmt_capture, 101 lines); the two `_ref_shadowed` per-token loops
(s335); the sibling-copy autoquote/callable sites (#266: 2-3 copies each);
two hand-strips of quote delimiters (#375).  Method: token/line-shingle
similarity over the perl (Perl one-liner or a small tool -- reuse
tools/lib if there is a shape), ranked by size x count; each cluster becomes
a candidate "extract to one sub" with the CLAUDE.md-11 test (does the family
already have a shared upstream point?).  Deliverable: a ranked worklist Opus
can execute mechanically (each extraction corpus-diff IDENTICAL, no emission
change, gate) -- CLAUDE.md 11 is the standing rule; this is its census.


PLAN WRITTEN s411 (Fable, 2026-08-18): docs/plan-one-compiler-s411.md (the simpler way: Phase R registry #383 -> A one expression compiler #384 -> B one seam function #385 -> C the 12 decline shapes #386; 3-5 sessions vs E5.1-E5.5 9-17; "one compiler" for v0.1 = one GENERATOR + one statement entry; E5.3 post-release, local first) and docs/dup-census-worklist-s411.md (#387 the extraction worklist; #388 the InterpScan consumers 2+3 port = the #1 duplicate family).  Tools: tools/dup-census.pl, tools/sub-call-census.pl.  USER decision 2026-08-18: structural first, not at any cost — the queue is the plan §6.  This task closes when Phases R-C are done (the census re-run then shows the deleted files gone).
subject: USER (s409): the two-compiler entanglement (88% expression fallback + 12 statement classes + the bucket dance + the double parse) "seems much too complex" -- NEXT FABLE SESSION: a plan to REORGANIZE it, asking first whether it can be done in a SIMPLER way than E5.1-E5.5 -- AND a comprehensive search for DOUBLED CODE (small bits extractable to subs)
